newsitem.title: USA: U.S. encouraged by N. Korean statement on Hunziker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. encouraged by N. Korean statement on Hunziker.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was somewhat encouraged by a North Korean statement describing the case of Carl Hunziker, an American arrested in North Korea on spying charges, as a humanitarian one.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Pyongyang issued a public statement on Monday "that was, we thought, somewhat encouraging."

The statement "mentioned that the Hunziker case is a humanitarian case, and we were pleased to see that language," Burns said. "We believe it is a humanitarian case, i.e. not an espionage case, and we still look for the early release of Mr Hunziker."

Hunziker, described by his family as a 26-year-old missionary, was arrested in North Korea on Aug. 24 after crossing from China. U.S. officials have ridiculed North Korean allegations that he was a spy.
Burns said the Swedish embassy in Pyongyang, which represents U.S. interests in North Korea and has visited Hunziker several times, had requested a further visit this week.
